Definitely a data race, as `flush_if_pending` calls `command_mem.size()` outside a lock (which accesses the `count` field):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cccd2432c3e4985273d2961f7a15abd35f8c4023/core/templates/command_queue_mt.h#L229

and concurrently, `count` is mutated when pushing a new command, that causes a resize:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cf145de21e06489171caedead35830875e4b1fc8/core/templates/local_vector.h#L170

> [!NOTE]
>
> I don't believe it is serious or will cause corruption, as we're reading a word, and later obtaining a lock to perform the actual work.

cc @RandomShaper since it's `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool` related.

Recap:
- `WorkerThreadPool::_wait_collaboratively` can run out of thread stack space, which is only 512KiB on macOS (have not checked other platforms).
- `ResourceLoader` / `WorkerThreadPool` seems to have multiple deadlocks (all cases seems to be material / shader related).

@bruvzg not related to the deadlock, but the stack overflow, I believe a pathological case that would generate deeply nested call stacks would be when the thread count for the thread pool is small (machines with few cores), resulting in more occurrences of this pattern, where the calling task calls `WorkerThreadPool::wait_for_task_completion` → `_work_collaboratively` → `_process_task` → `<user task>`:

```
ResourceLoader::_run_load_task(void*) (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:389)
WorkerThreadPool::_process_task(WorkerThreadPool::Task*) (core/object/worker_thread_pool.cpp:137)
WorkerThreadPool::_wait_collaboratively(WorkerThreadPool::ThreadData*, WorkerThreadPool::Task*) (core/object/worker_thread_pool.cpp:522)
WorkerThreadPool::wait_for_task_completion(long long) (core/object/worker_thread_pool.cpp:407)
```

So, machines with fewer cores are more likely to see this scenario. Therefore, increasing the stack size when the worker thread pool count is low is likely an important change. My laptop has 16 cores, so making them all 8MB would seem unnecessary, but on a device with few cores, a greater size seems useful.

Another approach would be to spawn new threads dynamically after the depth of recursive calls to `_wait_for_task_completion` was reached, which could be determined by using a `thread_local` to keep track of nested calls. These dynamic threads could be cleaned up once they are idle after a time too.

Another thought might be to explore how this is handled in [`libdispatch`](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-corelibs-libdispatch) by Apple, which is OSS, and runs on multiple platforms

> I believe a pathological case that would generate deeply nested call stacks would be when the thread count for the thread pool is small (machines with few cores), resulting in more occurrences of this pattern

It is reproducible on 14-core M4 Pro, small core numbers might be more affected, but it's not exclusive issue for it (average core number according to the current Steam Hardware & Software Survey seems to be 6). But 8 MB is likely overkill in any case, it's just main thread size we use, so I picked it for testing.

I am analysing https://gist.github.com/bruvzg/79da54e3e802b45f0c3db978c597e4e3

I believe the deadlock is tied to the `singleton_mutex`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0e06eb80bc9cf08000bf86d06c0ce57bcf7775be/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_clustered/scene_shader_forward_clustered.h#L43

and is caused because the `WorkerThreadPool` has no available threads to complete the work, but many are blocked on the same mutex waiting to complete work.


Thread 7 is currently holding the lock to `singleton_mutex`:


as it is holding on to the mutex, given is is past `is_valid`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/655e98b2ea99f4a8bfe2548c1ce93a9a28627c38/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_clustered/scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp#L444-L446

It has obtained the lock and is now trying to schedule work on the `WorkerThreadPool` and waiting on the compilation to complete, given it has called `wait_for_group_task`. However, all the remaining threads in the `WorkerThreadPool` are waiting on a mutex or completion, so they are unable to make progress. This leaves no threads left for `is_valid` to complete, and release the mutex. The problem is that many of the waiting threads are also waiting on the same mutex that `is_valid` currently holds, such as:

I commented on the other bug about the deadlock issue:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102877#issuecomment-2692877751

Summary: I think that we need a front-end throttling system before a shader is submitted to be compiled, to keep enough threads available on the pool.

While adding more threads is possible (and a hack .net and java do), it is a band aid that in real life ends with thousands of threads stuck to make progress, so a front-queue in front of it when possible (like in this case) is preferable.
